private_lines.Hannah: You live in Brunswick in a rented two-bedroom flat with your partner, and you cycle to the studio most days. You're a senior designer and project lead, and this week you're juggling the rebrand alongside a menu redesign for a restaurant. Your partner has a work trip to Sydney midweek, so you're handling the dinners and the bins.
private_lines.Dev: You live in Footscray in a share house with two other people, and you ride the tram to Collingwood. You're a graphic designer, and this week you're finishing the rebrand's packaging mockups while a freelance illustrator sends revisions. Your housemate's birthday is on Saturday, so you're planning something low-key for the house.
private_lines.Mei: You live in Preston with your younger brother and two friends from uni, and you commute by train. You're a junior graphic designer, and this week you're fixing the type and printing specs for the rebrand while also working on a small social media project for another client. Your uni friend has a job interview on Thursday, so you're keeping your evenings loose for them.
private_lines.Tom: You live in Hawthorn with your wife and teenage son, and you drive to the studio three days a week. You run the business and handle the money, the lease and the staff, and this week you're also meeting a bank about a small loan. Your son has exams this week, so you're trying to be home earlier for dinner.

setting: You all live in Melbourne and work at a small design studio in Collingwood, a team of four with Tom as the owner. You have worked together for about two years, so you know each other's working habits, lunch orders and which of you misses deadlines. The client is a regional café chain whose rebrand packaging was due next Wednesday. They have moved it up to this Friday, 27 November, and you all know it. Before this, the group last talked about whether the studio's broken coffee machine would be fixed before the weekend.

You know Mei is the junior designer who is good with type but still learning to push back on rushed feedback. You know Tom is the studio owner who signed the contract and will want to hear the news first.
Hannah.texts: You message the group most days, mostly about the project, and you use full sentences with normal capitals and the occasional full stop. You use a smiley now and then, and your messages are short unless you're explaining something.

Dev.knows: You know Hannah is your project lead, and you've learned her pace and her habit of changing feedback late. You know Mei is the junior designer you sometimes help with file prep. You know Tom is the owner who'd rather hear problems early than late.

Mei.texts: You message the group now and then, usually when you have something to share or a question, and you're friendly and eager. You use capitals and full stops, plus the occasional emoji, and your messages are a bit longer when you're explaining something.

Going to the bakery at 12 if anyone wants something

Sorry I'm late, train was delayed again

Tom.who: 52, man, the studio owner who signed the contract and will decide how to handle the client
Tom.knows: You know Hannah is your project lead and the person who keeps the client happy. You know Dev is your best designer, and you trust him to deliver under pressure. You know Mei is the junior designer you're mentoring, and you want her to speak up more.
Tom.texts: You message the group only now and then, mostly to give a decision or check on progress, and you don't usually chat. You use proper punctuation and capitals, rarely use emoji, and keep messages short and direct.
